materialFamilies: cast concrete with masked painted bands
objectClass.notes: A 0.25 x 0.9 x 0.2 m cast concrete stone with a semicircular arched crown, painted white over its top third, banded red beneath that, and left bare below. The ONLY prop in this signage set that is a single solid with no support and no joint anywhere.

reasoning: One solid, one material, one geometry, ONE draw call - under every ceiling this asset carries rather than at them, which is unusual in this set and is a consequence of the subject rather than of effort.

The painted bands WRAP the solid instead of sitting on a face, so the atlas needs a band column for the wall as well as a face region; every other prop in this set gets away with a single plain texel for everything that is not the front.
The arched crown is the whole silhouette: a kilometre stone with a flat top is a bollard.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: White painted crown over the arched top and upper third, down to the red band at 0.561 of height. Averaged from #ECF0F3 over 10799 lit bright px and #D9DCE0 over 6300 shaded bright px - a 19-luma spread across the two faces, so the albedo is taken between them rather than from the lit face alone.

Red band wrapping the whole stone from 0.431 to 0.561 of height. Measured #A32124 over 10800 lit px against #882322 over 4500 shaded px; the lit value is taken because the shaded face is fill-lit rather than key-lit and reads darker without being a different paint.
Large black distance numeral on the white crown, set right of centre on the face. Ink trimmed to #1B1F22 over 10415 sub-luma-70 px. SOLID FILL, never an outline.
Two black legend lines on the bare concrete below the band, a Thai province name over its Latin transliteration, set right of centre to match the numeral above.
Green-black algae darkening the lowest quarter of the concrete, measured #686554 over 9900 px - 45 luma below the clean body value and the strongest age cue on the prop.

A spalled patch on the front face below the legend where the render has broken away to expose darker aggregate. Painted into the atlas rather than modelled: it is a surface loss of a few millimetres and geometry for it would cost the prop's only spare axis.
Red paint flaking off the band's lower edge to show concrete beneath, concentrated on the left face where weather drives.

definitionOfDone: The arched crown reads as a semicircle in silhouette from every turntable azimuth, and the stone reads as a solid block rather than a plate.
The white crown and the red band WRAP the stone continuously and meet the front face exactly, with hard painted edges rather than blends.
Built to the declared 0.25 x 0.90 x 0.20 m.
One draw call, one material, one unique geometry and well under 800 triangles, measured in the harness.

declaredContract.rationale: A cast concrete stone is a static rigid body with no joint anywhere on it. One root pivot and zero sockets is the CORRECT answer, not a gap. This prop makes the point most cleanly of the eight: it has exactly one component, so a pivot per component would still be one, and that coincidence is not the reason - the reason is that nothing on it turns.
declaredContract.collider: box - honoured on the single component, and nearly exact rather than circumscribing
declaredContract.destructionRationale: The asset declares no destruction groups, so no component carries a fractureGroup and the prop does not come apart - which for a cast concrete stone is also what it would really do.

assumptions: back-and-side-faces: the three-quarter view shows two faces of the stone and neither carries lettering. The lettering is placed on ONE face only and the other three are left as plain banded concrete, which is what the reference supports rather than an invention.

band-heights: red band from 0.431 to 0.561 of height, read off the x=420 vertical scanline where the concrete-to-red edge falls at y=405 and the red-to-white edge at y=530 on a stone spanning y=78 to y=945.
arch-radius: a true semicircle on the stone's full width. The reference's crown is symmetric and springs from the full width, so a semicircle is a measurement rather than a simplification.
legend: representative Thai and Latin text for a province, not a transcription of the reference's particular stone. This is a kit prop.

coordinateFrame.front: +Z is the lettered face, the camera-facing side in the reference plate
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: metres. Origin at base-center: x=0 and z=0 on the stone's axis, y=0 at ground contact.

silhouette.boundingShape: A squat arch-topped block, roughly twice as tall as it is wide and nearly as deep as it is wide - the only prop in this set with real volume rather than a plate and a stick. Rebuilt from 0.25 x 0.90 x 0.20 to 0.49 x 0.90 x 0.42: the plate bounding box is 596 x 880 px across a three-quarter view and the Meshy proxy measures w/h 0.548, d/h 0.489, both of which the original 0.278 w/h ignored.

aspectRatios.note: 0.49 x 0.90 x 0.42 m declared. Width from the Meshy proxy bounds (w/h 0.548) at the 0.90 m declared height; depth from the band table's 5-95 percentile body depth of 0.46 of height rather than the proxy's 0.489 bbox extent, which includes the flared foot. Band table after the rebuild: mean |delta width| 0.0095, mean |delta depth| 0.026 at 0.44 deep, which is what moved it to 0.42.
0.42 / 0.49. The proxy bbox reads 0.89; its body percentile reads 0.84.
0.245 / 0.90 - a true semicircle on the full width. Shoulder at 0.728 of height; the plate shoulder scanlines at x=300 and x=640 read 0.74 and 0.71.

silhouette.symmetry: Bilateral about x=0 in geometry. The painted bands are symmetric; the legend is NOT - it sits right of centre - so the atlas must not be mirrored.
dominantCurves: the semicircular arched crown, the only curve on the prop and its entire silhouette identity
negativeSpaces: none. This is the only prop in the signage set with no negative space at all, which is why it reads as heavy where its siblings read as thin.

componentTree.name: Kilometre stone
componentTree.topologyRationale: A single cast-concrete solid: a rectangular block whose top is finished as a semicircular arch, extruded through its depth. One closed solid, not an assembly - there is no joint anywhere on this prop and nothing is bolted to anything, which is what separates it from every other prop in this signage set.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: ExtrudeGeometry over an arch-topped profile, 0.49 x 0.9, extruded 0.42 deep, with a 22 mm three-segment bevel on every edge. Every arris is ROLLED, not sharp: the plate's crown turns over in the depth axis as well as across the face - it is a rolled dome, not a barrel vault with a knife-edge perimeter - and the body's vertical corners are worn soft. `bevelSize` runs OUTWARD from the outline and the bevel hangs off both ends of the extrusion, so the shape is inset by the bevel on all four sides and the extrusion is shortened by two of them; the harness reads the bounds back as exactly 0.49 x 0.900 x 0.42. Normals are then smoothed with an angle-limited pass (62 degrees) so the bevel rounds over while the flat faces stay flat - unconditional averaging is the LatheGeometry mistake that shades a dark ring the turntable gate reads as a hole.

profile2D.note: 19 points: two bottom corners, straight sides up to y=0.655, then a 16-segment semicircular arch of radius 0.245 swept from angle 0 (right shoulder) through pi/2 (apex) to pi (LEFT shoulder). The earlier build swept -pi/2..pi/2, which is the RIGHT half of a circle - a quarter-round cusp on one side and no left shoulder at all - and rendered visibly lop-sided. The arch IS this prop's silhouette.

geometryDescriptor.uvStrategy: authored - a two-region atlas. The FRONT cap takes a full face region carrying the painted bands and the legend; the wall and the back cap take a narrow band COLUMN whose v is the same height fraction, so the red band and the white crown wrap continuously round the stone and meet the front face exactly. This is what lets one material paint a banded solid rather than a plate with a printed front.
geometryDescriptor.segmentRationale: 16 arch segments on a 0.245 m radius and one segment everywhere else. The crown is the only curve on the prop.

pivot.notes: The root pivot, at base-center. This prop has exactly ONE component and ONE pivot, and that is the correct count: a cast concrete stone has no moving parts and nothing attaches to it.

collider.notes: Declared collider for this asset is `box`, and unlike the post-mounted signs in this set the proxy is nearly EXACT: the stone is a rectangular solid apart from its arched crown, so the box is the shape rather than a circumscription of it.

surfaceDetail.normalPattern: bumpMap from a height atlas painted alongside the albedo, at half its resolution
surfaceDetail.edgeWearPattern: clustered polygon flakes off both edges of the red band; ragged chipping round the foot
surfaceDetail.notes: The atlas is a band COLUMN plus a face region with a guard gutter between them. The column used to be sampled at ONE u by every side wall and the back - a single texel column stretched across 0.42 m of stone, so nothing on those faces could vary horizontally and every wash arrived as a full-width horizontal band. It is 0.30 of the atlas now and the walls map their own horizontal position into it: a side wall along z, the back cap and the crown along x.

colorMaterialRecipe.notes: An ordered VERTICAL ramp measured up from the foot, with hard edges at both band boundaries: this is masked paint on cast concrete, so the boundaries are lines and not blends. The stops are doubled at each edge. Unlike every other prop in this set the bands WRAP the whole solid rather than sitting on a printed face, which is why the atlas carries a band column for the wall as well as a face region.

materials.name: Cast concrete with masked painted bands

albedo.samplingNotes: White base colour because every band and stain is delivered by the atlas assigned after material construction; a tint here would multiply into all five colours at once.

colorVariation.pattern: authored-bands over vertically-elongated stain drift, formwork striation and aggregate grain
colorVariation.notes: The bands are authored; everything on top of them is weathering, and its amplitude is MEASURED rather than chosen. A matched 110x120 px window on the plate's shaded body reads luma 155 with sd 23; the flat build read the same window at 111 with sd 5, and the shipped build reads 135 with sd 10 on the shaded face and 148 with sd 18 on the key-lit one. The two drift poles are spread wide and biased LIGHT (#7A7663 luma 116 and #DCD8C6 luma 214, compositing over the base to about 132..186) because the spread has to be bought without pushing any texel toward the turntable gate's backdrop luma of 58.

roughness.localResponse: Chalky and fully matte - the highest roughness of the eight props. Cast concrete and masked paint both scatter completely; there is no tight highlight anywhere on this reference, and the two faces at right angles differ by only 2 luma on the body, which is what a fully diffuse surface under strong fill does. Relief arrives as a bumpMap rather than as roughness variation: the height atlas is painted alongside the albedo off the SAME draw streams, so its grain, striation, chips and spall land on the marks the picture shows. It ships at half the albedo's resolution - relief is low-frequency where it matters, and two full 1024 RGBA textures is 11 MB of VRAM on a kit aimed at low-end integrated GPUs.

metalness.notes: Concrete and paint are both dielectric. No metal anywhere on this prop, which makes it the only one of the eight with no galvanised material at all.

ambientOcclusion.notes: A convex solid with no cavity for AO to find, and baking any into base colour is what the material pass forbids. The 22 mm rolled arris is GEOMETRY and shades itself; the only recess on the prop is the spall, and its shadow is painted into the albedo and the height atlas rather than into an AO channel.

chips.where: the red band's lower and upper edges, and scattered across its face
chips.evidence: The plate's band is the most damaged surface on the stone: paint lifted off both edges in clustered irregular flakes exposing the concrete beneath. Each chip is an 8-sided polygon with a #8E2226 rim where the film has lifted. They are wider than they are tall - the first tuning made them 0.07..0.33 of the band's height and hung a row of white icicles off the red.

chips.where: the bottom 6 per cent of the stone, all round
chips.evidence: The plate's foot is ragged rather than a clean cast edge.

spalls.where: the front face, 0.115 of the face width from its left arris
spalls.evidence: Re-measured off the plate: the void spans y=735..870 on a stone spanning y=72..952, i.e. 0.093 to 0.247 of height. The previous build placed it at 0.21 and half that size. Painted rather than modelled - it is a surface loss of a few millimetres - but it carries relief in the height atlas, and it is painted from the OUTSIDE IN: a soft shadow spilling onto the wall, a #6B6047 void, then a small patch of lit #C8C1AE aggregate low inside it. A hole is darker than the wall it is in, and filling the void with pale aggregate is what made the first two tunings read as a sticker.

dirt.notes: Three separate marks, not one smudge. (1) A standing ramp from the band to the foot, nearly flat over the top half - the plate's body only collapses in its lowest fifth, and a ramp that starts at the band renders the whole body 44 luma too dark. (2) Rain runs biased to the band's lower edge, which is the drip line on the plate. (3) Algae over the lowest fifth as a gradient PLUS speck clusters thickening downward; a gradient alone is a smudge. The algae is #6F7659 - green-chroma at luma 113 - rather than the previous neutral #686554, because the hole gate reads a back-lit face at about 0.55 of its painted luma against a backdrop at 58 and a neutral grey that dark is a hole the gate has to guess about.

localOverrides.region: the arched crown and the upper third of the stone
localOverrides.notes: Averaged from #ECF0F3 over 10799 lit bright px at (380,120,120,90) and #D9DCE0 over 6300 shaded bright px at (280,200,70,90). A 19-luma spread across the two faces, so the albedo is taken BETWEEN them rather than from the lit face alone - the same reasoning that put the red band's value on its lit face is reversed here, because the crown's shaded reading is fill-lit white rather than key-lit.

localOverrides.region: the band wrapping the stone from 0.472 to 0.617 of height
localOverrides.notes: Trimmed mean #A32124 over the full 10800 px of (560,380,180,60) on the lit face; the shaded face at (270,400,90,50) returns #882322 over 4500 px. The lit value is taken because the shaded face is fill-lit rather than key-lit and reads darker without being a different paint. Band edges re-read on the x=420 scanline of the shaded face: white-to-red at y=409 (0.617 of height from the foot) and red-to-concrete at y=537 (0.472), on a stone spanning y=72 to y=952. The first build had 0.431-0.561, both edges 0.05 low, which put the white crown over 44 per cent of the stone instead of 38.

localOverrides.region: the bare concrete below the red band
localOverrides.notes: Trimmed mean #98917F over 25200 px lit and #988F7A over 12600 px shaded - within 2 luma of each other. That agreement across two faces at right angles is why this albedo could be taken directly rather than de-lit.

localOverrides.region: the lowest quarter of the concrete, heaviest at the corners
localOverrides.notes: Trimmed mean #686554 over 9900 px at (250,800,90,110). 45 luma below the clean body value and the strongest age cue on the prop. A saturation-band scan up the stone reads 0 per cent everywhere above y=330 and 34 per cent at y=360, confirming the growth is confined to the foot.

localOverrides.region: the distance numeral on the crown and both legend lines on the concrete
localOverrides.notes: Trimmed mean of the 10415 sub-luma-70 px of (560,220,180,140). The whole-crop mean was far lighter because the crop's bright half is the white crown bouncing across a hard boundary, not ink.

shaderNotes: Prefer MeshPhysicalMaterial when clearcoat, sheen, transmission, or thin-surface response is observed; otherwise use MeshStandardMaterial-compatible PBR channels.
Generate albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO independently; never alias albedo into roughness.
Use normal/bump/displacement only when they map to observed surface relief.
Use displacement geometry when the observed relief changes the close-up silhouette; texture-only relief is insufficient there.
materials.notes: Replace with image-derived color, roughness, noise, and edge-wear notes.

evidence: The generator's five synthesised canvases are what this declaration skips, and they are still skipped: everything this prop shows arrives on ONE canvas atlas pair assigned AFTER material construction, which the declaration does not touch. Letting the generator synthesise a texture set here would additionally force color to white and roughness to 1 and read both from the generated maps, discarding the measured #98917F that makes this stone concrete rather than grey.

Reference plate, concrete body at (560,600,180,140) and (270,600,90,140): 25200 and 12600 px trimming to #98917F and #988F7A - within 2 luma across two faces at right angles. That agreement is why the BASE albedo could be taken directly; it is not a claim that the surface is flat, and the same plate reads luma variance 0.071 over the whole stone against a flat build's 0.050.
Reference plate, red band at (560,380,180,60): 10800 px trimming to #A32124. Masked paint over cast concrete.
Reference plate, white crown at (380,120,120,90): 10799 of 10800 px pass a bright filter, trimming to #ECF0F3.

Measured cost: five synthesised canvases at 1024 would cost roughly 1.9 s inside createObjectModel. The atlas pair that replaces them is Path2D fills, not a per-pixel loop, and the whole factory builds in 180 ms measured by render-model.mjs.

Body #98917F measured over 25200 lit px and #988F7A over 12600 shaded px - within 2 luma across two faces at right angles, which is why this albedo could be taken directly rather than de-lit. featureReviews.evidence: A 16-segment semicircular crown of radius 0.245 swept 0..pi from the right shoulder over the apex to the LEFT shoulder, springing from the stone's full 0.49 m width at 0.655 m. The first build swept -pi/2..pi/2 - the RIGHT half of a circle - and shipped a quarter-round cusp hanging below the right shoulder with no left shoulder at all; its review claimed it read as a semicircle at every azimuth, and the 0/90 turntable frames show it did not. Now symmetric at 0, 90, 180 and 270, and the shoulder height agrees with the plate's x=300 and x=640 scanlines (0.74 and 0.71 of height against the built 0.728).

Rebuilt from 0.25 x 0.90 x 0.20 to 0.49 x 0.90 x 0.42. Harness bounds match exactly. Band table against the Meshy proxy (feet=0, height=1, 5-95 pct surface samples): mean |delta width| 0.0095, mean |delta depth| 0.0065, every body band within 0.005 of the proxy's 0.547 width. The first build's w/h of 0.278 was HALF the proxy's 0.548 and the earlier review only compared depth-over-width, where two wrong numbers agreed. Depth taken from the proxy's body percentile (0.46 of height) rather than its bbox extent (0.489), which includes the flared foot.

Bands re-read on the x=420 scanline of the plate's shaded face: white-to-red at y=409 and red-to-concrete at y=537 on a stone spanning y=72..952, i.e. 0.617 and 0.472 of height. The first build had 0.431-0.561 - the two edge readings were transposed and both landed 0.05 low, which put white over 44 per cent of the stone instead of 38. Bands still wrap continuously and meet the front face exactly because v is the height fraction for every vertex. The legend re-placed off the plate too: numeral centred at 0.775 of height, Thai line at 0.41, Latin line at 0.33, all at 0.54 of the face width, with glyph heights 0.12 / 0.056 / 0.036 m.

Albedo, roughness and algae carried over unchanged (#98917F body over 25200 lit px, #686554 algae over the lowest quarter, roughness 0.85). The comparison sheet at the corrected proportions shows the plate's body is heavily stained and mottled over its whole height while the build's is one flat tone above the algae gradient, and the spalled patch and paint flaking are painted graphics. Scored below the earlier 0.84 because that score was read off a slender post whose face was a third the area; at the true width the flatness is the largest remaining gap on this prop and is the surface pass's work, not this correction's.

visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Shape now matches the plate at every azimuth; the remaining gap is a flat concrete body against a heavily stained one, which is surface work.

featureReviews.evidence: The named gap of the previous review, scored 0.76 there because the body was one flat tone above a foot gradient while the plate is stained over its whole height. It is now six layers on a canvas atlas pair painted off shared draw streams: a standing ramp, vertically elongated stain drift, formwork striation, aggregate grain, algae speck clusters at the foot and ragged foot chipping - with a bumpMap painted alongside the albedo so the relief lands on the marks the picture shows. MEASURED against the plate on a matched 110x120 px window of the key-lit body: plate luma 155 sd 23, flat build 138 sd 12.6, this build 154 sd 19.3. The deterministic material comparator moves deltaE00 2.96 -> 2.44, baseColor 0.941 -> 0.951 and directionalResponse 0.839 -> 0.944. Two things still short of the plate: the shaded side faces read 126 against the plate's 155, which is the harness's key direction rather than the albedo (the key-lit face matches to 1 luma); and horizontalGradient reaches 0.032 against the plate's 0.058, which is texel density - the face region carries 1379 px/m and the plate is a much larger subject in frame.

Every edge is a 22 mm three-segment bevel. The plate's crown turns over in the DEPTH axis as well as across the face - it is a rolled dome, not a barrel vault with a knife-edge perimeter - and the previous build's prismatic extrude with bevelEnabled false showed a hard silhouette edge at every azimuth. Normals are smoothed with an angle-limited pass at 62 degrees so the bevel rounds over while the flat faces stay flat; unconditional averaging is the LatheGeometry mistake that shades a dark ring the turntable gate reads as a hole. bevelSize runs OUTWARD, so the shape is inset by it on all four sides and the extrusion shortened by two - measured, not assumed: the first attempt left the shape at full size and the harness read bounds of 0.534 x 0.944. Bounds now read exactly 0.490 x 0.900 x 0.420. Arch segments 16 -> 24. 72 -> 428 triangles of 2000.

The previous build had fourteen axis-aligned rectangles along the band's lower edge, which rendered as a sawtooth graphic. It is now 13 clusters of 4-11 eight-sided polygons on BOTH edges and scattered across the face, each with a #8E2226 rim where the paint film has lifted, wider than they are tall. And the body sheds FROM them: 45 per cent of the drip runs start directly under a lower-edge cluster at 1.25x strength, which is what ties the two surfaces together on the plate and is why the band is painted before the body in paintWrapped.

Re-measured off the plate: the void spans y=735..870 on a stone spanning y=72..952, i.e. 0.093 to 0.247 of height, so it is centred at 0.17 and is 0.135 of the height tall - the previous build had it at 0.21 and half that size, as a flat grey ellipse. It is painted from the OUTSIDE IN now: a soft shadow spilling onto the wall, a #6B6047 void, then a small patch of lit #C8C1AE aggregate low inside it, with a matching recess in the height atlas. A hole is darker than the wall it is in; filling the void with pale aggregate is what made the first two attempts read as a sticker.

The atlas column was sampled at ONE u by every side wall and the back - a single texel column stretched across 0.42 m of stone - so nothing on three of the four faces could vary horizontally and every wash arrived as a full-width horizontal band. It is 0.30 of the atlas now, with a guard gutter flood-filled rather than left transparent, and the walls map their own horizontal position into it (a side wall along z, the back cap and crown along x). Mark sizes are then scaled by 0.40 and counts divided by it, because the column carries 1.37 mm per texel against the face's 0.54 and the same fraction is a mark 2.5x larger in the world.

The Thai line rendered as six tofu boxes in the harness and in the thumbnail it writes. The image carried fonts-liberation and nothing else, so fontconfig had no Thai answer at all - on a prop whose whole subject is a Thai road sign. fonts-thai-tlwg is in the Dockerfile's base stage now (about 5 MB), and the face stack names Loma and Garuda after Noto Sans Thai so a browser that has Noto still gets Noto. Verified in the render.

reviewHistory.summary: Single-component cast concrete stone built to the declared 0.250 x 0.900 x 0.200 m. 56 triangles of 800, 1 draw call of 2, 1 material of 2, 1 unique geometry of 2, one texture - UNDER every ceiling rather than at it, which is a property of the subject and not a credit to the build: a kilometre stone is one solid with no support, so there is nothing to merge and nothing to split. The passes were worked as ONE build with the deterministic gates run once over the finished prop rather than per pass; the per-pass content is real but the per-pass evidence is not. This is the only prop of the eight with no metal on it, no negative space, and paint that WRAPS the solid rather than sitting on a printed face - which is why its atlas carries a band column for the wall as well as a face region, where every sibling gets away with one plain texel.

featureReviews.evidence: A 16-segment semicircular crown of radius 0.245 swept 0..pi from the right shoulder over the apex to the LEFT shoulder, springing from the stone's full 0.49 m width at 0.655 m. The first build swept -pi/2..pi/2 - the RIGHT half of a circle - and shipped a quarter-round cusp hanging below the right shoulder with no left shoulder at all; its review claimed it read as a semicircle at every azimuth, and the 0/90 turntable frames show it did not. Now symmetric at 0, 90, 180 and 270, and the shoulder height agrees with the plate's x=300 and x=640 scanlines (0.74 and 0.71 of height against the built 0.728).

Rebuilt from 0.25 x 0.90 x 0.20 to 0.49 x 0.90 x 0.42. Harness bounds match exactly. Band table against the Meshy proxy (feet=0, height=1, 5-95 pct surface samples): mean |delta width| 0.0095, mean |delta depth| 0.0065, every body band within 0.005 of the proxy's 0.547 width. The first build's w/h of 0.278 was HALF the proxy's 0.548 and the earlier review only compared depth-over-width, where two wrong numbers agreed. Depth taken from the proxy's body percentile (0.46 of height) rather than its bbox extent (0.489), which includes the flared foot.

Bands re-read on the x=420 scanline of the plate's shaded face: white-to-red at y=409 and red-to-concrete at y=537 on a stone spanning y=72..952, i.e. 0.617 and 0.472 of height. The first build had 0.431-0.561 - the two edge readings were transposed and both landed 0.05 low, which put white over 44 per cent of the stone instead of 38. Bands still wrap continuously and meet the front face exactly because v is the height fraction for every vertex. The legend re-placed off the plate too: numeral centred at 0.775 of height, Thai line at 0.41, Latin line at 0.33, all at 0.54 of the face width, with glyph heights 0.12 / 0.056 / 0.036 m.

Albedo, roughness and algae carried over unchanged (#98917F body over 25200 lit px, #686554 algae over the lowest quarter, roughness 0.85). The comparison sheet at the corrected proportions shows the plate's body is heavily stained and mottled over its whole height while the build's is one flat tone above the algae gradient, and the spalled patch and paint flaking are painted graphics. Scored below the earlier 0.84 because that score was read off a slender post whose face was a third the area; at the true width the flatness is the largest remaining gap on this prop and is the surface pass's work, not this correction's.

(1) The arch was swept -pi/2..pi/2 - the right HALF of a circle - so the crown was a one-sided cusp; now swept 0..pi over the full width, 16 segments. (2) The declared section 0.25 x 0.20 m was a slender post; the plate's bounding box (596 x 880 px) and the Meshy proxy (w/h 0.548) both show a squat block, so the section is now 0.49 x 0.42 at the same 0.90 m height. The band table against the proxy reads mean |delta width| 0.0095 and |delta depth| 0.0065. (3) Band edges were 0.05 low (0.431-0.561), re-read off the x=420 scanline as 0.472-0.617; legend re-placed to match. 72 triangles of 2000, 1 draw call of 2, 1 material of 2, 1 geometry of 2, one 512 atlas. featureReviews.evidence: The named gap of the previous review, scored 0.76 there because the body was one flat tone above a foot gradient while the plate is stained over its whole height. It is now six layers on a canvas atlas pair painted off shared draw streams: a standing ramp, vertically elongated stain drift, formwork striation, aggregate grain, algae speck clusters at the foot and ragged foot chipping - with a bumpMap painted alongside the albedo so the relief lands on the marks the picture shows. MEASURED against the plate on a matched 110x120 px window of the key-lit body: plate luma 155 sd 23, flat build 138 sd 12.6, this build 154 sd 19.3. The deterministic material comparator moves deltaE00 2.96 -> 2.44, baseColor 0.941 -> 0.951 and directionalResponse 0.839 -> 0.944. Two things still short of the plate: the shaded side faces read 126 against the plate's 155, which is the harness's key direction rather than the albedo (the key-lit face matches to 1 luma); and horizontalGradient reaches 0.032 against the plate's 0.058, which is texel density - the face region carries 1379 px/m and the plate is a much larger subject in frame.

Every edge is a 22 mm three-segment bevel. The plate's crown turns over in the DEPTH axis as well as across the face - it is a rolled dome, not a barrel vault with a knife-edge perimeter - and the previous build's prismatic extrude with bevelEnabled false showed a hard silhouette edge at every azimuth. Normals are smoothed with an angle-limited pass at 62 degrees so the bevel rounds over while the flat faces stay flat; unconditional averaging is the LatheGeometry mistake that shades a dark ring the turntable gate reads as a hole. bevelSize runs OUTWARD, so the shape is inset by it on all four sides and the extrusion shortened by two - measured, not assumed: the first attempt left the shape at full size and the harness read bounds of 0.534 x 0.944. Bounds now read exactly 0.490 x 0.900 x 0.420. Arch segments 16 -> 24. 72 -> 428 triangles of 2000.

The previous build had fourteen axis-aligned rectangles along the band's lower edge, which rendered as a sawtooth graphic. It is now 13 clusters of 4-11 eight-sided polygons on BOTH edges and scattered across the face, each with a #8E2226 rim where the paint film has lifted, wider than they are tall. And the body sheds FROM them: 45 per cent of the drip runs start directly under a lower-edge cluster at 1.25x strength, which is what ties the two surfaces together on the plate and is why the band is painted before the body in paintWrapped.

Re-measured off the plate: the void spans y=735..870 on a stone spanning y=72..952, i.e. 0.093 to 0.247 of height, so it is centred at 0.17 and is 0.135 of the height tall - the previous build had it at 0.21 and half that size, as a flat grey ellipse. It is painted from the OUTSIDE IN now: a soft shadow spilling onto the wall, a #6B6047 void, then a small patch of lit #C8C1AE aggregate low inside it, with a matching recess in the height atlas. A hole is darker than the wall it is in; filling the void with pale aggregate is what made the first two attempts read as a sticker.

The atlas column was sampled at ONE u by every side wall and the back - a single texel column stretched across 0.42 m of stone - so nothing on three of the four faces could vary horizontally and every wash arrived as a full-width horizontal band. It is 0.30 of the atlas now, with a guard gutter flood-filled rather than left transparent, and the walls map their own horizontal position into it (a side wall along z, the back cap and crown along x). Mark sizes are then scaled by 0.40 and counts divided by it, because the column carries 1.37 mm per texel against the face's 0.54 and the same fraction is a mark 2.5x larger in the world.

The Thai line rendered as six tofu boxes in the harness and in the thumbnail it writes. The image carried fonts-liberation and nothing else, so fontconfig had no Thai answer at all - on a prop whose whole subject is a Thai road sign. fonts-thai-tlwg is in the Dockerfile's base stage now (about 5 MB), and the face stack names Loma and Garuda after Noto Sans Thai so a browser that has Noto still gets Noto. Verified in the render.
